title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting Elicits Reasoning in Large Language Models
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS)
problem: Large language models often struggle with complex reasoning tasks such as arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic reasoning.
method: Chain-of-thought prompting, where few-shot exemplars include intermediate natural language reasoning steps leading to the final answer.
key_results: Chain-of-thought prompting significantly improves reasoning performance across arithmetic, commonsense, and symbolic tasks in large language models.
Prompting PaLM 540B with eight chain-of-thought exemplars achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on GSM8K, surpassing finetuned GPT-3 with a verifier.
limitations: Emulating human thought processes does not prove the neural network is actually reasoning.
Chain-of-thought reasoning only emerges at large model scales (typically around 100B parameters).
There is no guarantee of correct reasoning paths, which can lead to incorrect answers.
future_work: Improve factual generations of language models.
Explore how to induce reasoning capabilities in smaller models.
Evaluate chain-of-thought prompting on more diverse tasks such as machine translation.
key_claims: Chain-of-thought prompting elicits complex reasoning abilities in large language models without requiring finetuning.
Chain-of-thought reasoning is an emergent ability of model scale, appearing mostly in models with roughly 100B or more parameters.
Chain-of-thought prompting facilitates out-of-domain length generalization for symbolic reasoning tasks.
